page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7se.xlarge is a compute-oriented virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor featuring an x86_64 architecture with 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs via multithreading. Hardware cache includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (foundation and VNNI), alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is allocated 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

The configuration does not bundle local storage, relying on external network-attached block volumes for persistent disk storage. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Memory throughput benchmarks show 30.35 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 25.29 GB/sec for uncached write operations, reflecting standard dual-channel server memory characteristics.

Benchmark evaluation shows average single-threaded efficiency alongside multi-threaded metrics constrained by the physical core count. The instance recorded 1556.0 on Geekbench single-core, 1883.99 on stress-ng single-core, and 27.97 GB/sec in gzip compression. Multi-threaded processing registered 3343.0 on Geekbench and 3871.28 on stress-ng. PassMark encryption testing reached 3658.3, aided by integrated cryptographic hardware acceleration, while static web serving throughput reached 6.33 GB/sec and Redis SET performance delivered 3.95 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c7se.xlarge offers dedicated compute resources without the overhead of massive memory allocations or local NVMe storage arrays. It is best suited for compute-focused entry tiers, small-scale microservices, static web serving, and basic proxy routing.

Configured with 2 physical cores and 4 dedicated vCPUs, it pairs 8.0 GB of RAM with a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, operating entirely with external network-attached volumes. Synthetic testing reflects average single-core capabilities, registering 1556.0 on Geekbench single-core and 27.97 GB/sec in gzip compression, while overall multi-threaded throughput is constrained by the two physical core count. Hardware encryption support via AES and SHA-NI delivers stable cryptographic metrics, complemented by a static web serving throughput of 6.33 GB/sec. Given its 1:2 core-to-memory ratio and lack of local NVMe storage, the ecs.c7se.xlarge serves entry-tier application tiers, lightweight web serving, and modular backend microservices.
